title.narrative: Romania Shelterbelts and Sustainable Agriculture Biocarbon Fund Project

description.narrative: The Romanian government promotes the establishment of forest shelterbelts near settlementscomma on crop land and along irrigation systemscomma as a way to improve microclimates and control droughtscomma which have become more prevalent over the recent decades. These objectives are among those of Law No. 289 .Forest Shelterbelts. (May 15comma 2002)comma Governmental Resolution No. 547 (May 17comma 2003) on the establishment of a national system of shelterbeltscomma and the draft .National Strategy and Action Programme Concerning Desertificationcomma Land Degradation and Drought Prevention and Control. (2000). To support these objectivescomma and also mitigate global climate changecomma the BioCarbon Fund would purchase ERs generated by 2comma000 ha of forest shelterbelts (windbreaks) in eight counties (Calarasicomma Constantacomma Doljcomma Galaticomma Giurgiucomma Ialomitacomma Oltcomma Teleorman). In order to establish these 2comma000 hacomma about 67comma000 ha of agricultural land must be foundcomma since these shelterbeltscomma ranging from 10 meters to 30 meters in widthcomma typically cover 3 percent of agricultural land. Shelterbelts protect against wind and soil erosion. In additioncomma shelterbelts increase moisture retentioncomma enhance biological diversitycomma and improve microclimatic conditions. Ultimately shelterbelts improve soil productivity and agricultural yields. Shelterbelts are an effective store of carbon as they build dense strips of vegetationcomma while they do not take land away from production. Depending on the preferences of local communities on whose land the project would be implementedcomma measures could also be supported that enhance carbon sequestration through better agricultural techniques such as reduced tillagecomma while also achieving other environmental benefits. Species planted would include treescomma e.g. Robinia pseudoacaciacomma Gleditschia triachantoscomma Prunus cerasiferacomma Prunus aviumcomma Juglans regiacomma Eleagnus angustifoliacomma and possibly Quercus sp.comma and shrubscomma e.g. Rosa canina and Crataegus monogyna. Compared to the PCF afforestation projectcomma the cost of establishing shelterbelts is expected to be lower per ha: (1) the land is less degraded than the land afforested under the PCF project; and (2) more carbon would be sequestered per hacomma increasing reimbursements to the financier. Financing Financial resources to plant the shelterbelts would be found from a variety of sourcescomma includingcomma possiblycomma the national budget through the Ministry of Agriculturecomma Forestscomma Waters and Environment.s Land Reclamation Fundcomma the World Bank.s loan to the Irrigation Rehabilitation and Reform Projectcomma the Global Environmental Facility (GEF).s grant for the Agricultural Pollution Control Projectcomma and local communities themselves. The proceeds of the sales of ERs to the BioCarbon Fund would then reimburse the financiers on an annual basis proportionally and to their share of the project costs and depending on the level of carbon sequestration realized by the project. No Bank budget would be involved in the preparation or the supervision of the project. A part of the preparation costs would be borne by the PHRD Grant and the Ministry of Agriculturecomma Forestscomma Waters and Environmentcomma while the balance of these costs and the supervision costs would be borne with the BioCarbon Fund. Institutional Arrangements This project will need a different implementation arrangement than the first PCF Afforestation project to the extent that communities are more involved in this new projectcomma primarily because they will decide whether to establish forest shelter belts on their own landcomma not state-owned land as in the PCF project. The project may benefit from implementation arrangements piloted by various previous projectscomma in particular the Irrigation Rehabilitation Project and the Agricultural Pollution Control Project. For instancecomma the communities and budget resources could finance establishment of the shelterbelts with technical assistance from the National Forest Administration (NFA). The ER purchase agreement could be signed by the Ministry of Agriculturecomma Forestscomma Waters and Environmentcomma who would serve as intermediary between the BioCarbon Fund and local communities.
